findings.title: Race in new concurrency test: reader thread is never joined
findings.body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a reader thread but never joins it. The assertion on caughtExceptions runs immediately after deletedAll.set(true), so exceptions thrown by the last in-flight read (exactly the NPE window the fix targets) can be recorded after the assertion and silently ignored, making the test both flaky and able to pass even when the bug is present. The thread also leaks beyond the test and busy-loops calling the admin API without any sleep, consuming CPU. Join the thread (with a timeout) before asserting.

findings.title: Remaining NPE paths via modelSupplier.get() not guarded
findings.body: Only getSubGroupsCount() was hardened against a null delegate. getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults), getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults) and getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults) (lines 256, 262, 268) still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) directly, so when the group is concurrently removed from the database the supplier returns null and the same NullPointerException reported in #40368 is thrown from those paths. They should handle a null model consistently (e.g. return Stream.empty() or throw a meaningful model exception).

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() may now return null
findings.body: getSubGroupsCount() returns null when the backing group has been removed. GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() previously never returned null, and callers that unbox the Long (e.g. arithmetic or long assignment) will now throw NullPointerException instead of the previous NPE location; GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount will also produce a representation with a null subGroupCount. Consider returning 0L or documenting the nullability on the interface.
